To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) extended Rayleigh-type expressions were derived to account in principle for multiple competing degradation processes, (ii) the derived equations were applied successfully to a previously published data set, (iii) the equations enabled quantification of the relative share that two competing pathways had on aerobic degradation of 1,2-DCE in laboratory batch experiments, (iv) the results of this study are of importance for quantification of biodegradation in natural settings where several competing degradation pathways can occur simultaneously, and (

the environmental α values for 1,2-DCE and 1,2,3-trichloropropane (TCP) during biodegradation of 1,2-DCP and 1,3-DCP, respectively, are not constant and that this behavior can be explained by the existence of two degradation pathways with different half-saturation concentrations.

(i) the Rayleigh equation is extended to allow for multiple competing degradation reactions, (ii) the environmental or apparent isotopic fractionation is a function of the fractionating factors and rate constants of each competing degradation pathway and (iii) non-Rayleigh behavior of the apparent isotopic fractionating factor is predicted if the Monod kinetics is applied and the half-saturations constants of the competing degradation pathways differ.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel methods to quantify biodegradation in environmental systems, and the application of these methods to environmental systems.
the quantification of the contribution of competing degradation pathways to the overall degradation of 1,2-DCE and 1,2-DCAs, which was not previously possible.

the development of novel analytical methods for the determination of trace amounts of organic compounds, and with the elucidation of the chemical and biological processes involved in the fate and transport of these compounds in the environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Rayleigh equation is a very good approximation to the extended Rayleigh equations for a single degradation pathway.

, in the case of multiple competing degradation pathways, the Rayleigh equation should not be applied to the total substrate concentration but rather to the individual concentration fractions of each competing pathway.
the extended equations derived in this study are applicable for the quantification of biodegradation and the determination of the share of different pathways in the biodegradation process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed a new tool to quantify the extent of substrate biodegradation.
we derived a new equation for quantification of biodegradation based on isotope ratios.
the Rayleigh equation is a special case of a more general equation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Rayleigh equation can be applied to quantify biodegradation in the presence of competing isotope fractionating degradation pathways.

isotope data alone can be used to estimate the share that two or more competing degradation pathways have on the biodegradation of a compound, and that the isotope data can be used to identify which of the competing pathways is dominant.
it is not sufficient to measure the isotope ratio of a substrate in order to quantify biodegradation.
